text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: routing/ingress SLO breach — us-west-2. p99 2.1s (SLO 1.0s). Affected: streaming responses + long-tail token latency. Triggered by routing-policy rollout at ~19:23 UTC. Paging oncall @channel
Alex Chen: Ack, I'm oncall. grabbing initial graphs.
Ryan SRE: Looking at grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/routers/router-latency. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 600ms, p99 at 2.1s. We see a sudden step at 19:23 matching the policy rollout.
Mira Patel: I can see the rollout in deploy logs: PR #4126 flipped `zone_affinity: enabled` and adjusted consistent-hash weights. That commit reduced pool weight for pool-gpu-a by ~30%.
Dan O'Neill: If weight for pool-gpu-a dropped and traffic sticky to hash ranges stayed, that would shift hot keys into fewer nodes -> hot queueing. Also seeing increase in streaming stalls (connections held open longer).
Alex Chen: Any visible error spike? customers reporting timeouts?
Ryan SRE: Errors up slightly (5xx retry spikes for streaming connectors). Downstream retry probably amplifying tail. Here's a query of router logs: ```
# sample
select count(*) from router_logs where status >= 500 and ts > now() - 10m group by 1m;
```
Mira Patel: The rollout was auto-approved by the release bot; guardrails didn't catch >20% capacity shift. I'll block any further rollouts for routing-policy until we triage.
Dan O'Neill: Mitigation options: 1) increase pool-gpu-a weight back to previous value, 2) divert traffic off hot hash ranges (temporary weight-shift), 3) enable fallback to dedicated-cold pool. I recommend fast weight bump to spread load.
Alex Chen: I'll apply weight bump and force immediate reconverge. Posting admin commands.
Alex Chen: ```
# router-admin
POST /admin/route_weights
{ "pool": "pool-gpu-a", "weight": 140 }
```
Alex Chen: Done — issued POST at 19:39 UTC.
Ryan SRE: Seeing p95 improve to ~250ms within 2 min. p99 still at ~1.3s. Streaming stalls decreasing but not gone; looks like KV cache churn is still high for a subset of shards.
Dan O'Neill: We should drain the three hottest nodes and mark them `maintenance` so new connections don't land there. I'll trigger maintenance tag on node-24/25/26.
Dan O'Neill: ```
# k8s maintenance
kubectl label node node-24 maintenance=true
kubectl label node node-25 maintenance=true
kubectl label node node-26 maintenance=true
```
Mira Patel: Note: draining will drop some in-flight streaming sessions -> accept some 499s while we rebalance. We need to call out customers who might have active long polls.
Liz Product: Can you estimate customer impact? Which customers showed elevated retries/timeouts?
Ryan SRE: Quick hit: three accounts (acct-17, acct-42, acct-88) saw >5% increase in retries and ~10-15% of streaming sessions timed out between 19:23-19:45 UTC. No data loss, just higher latencies and client retries.
Alex Chen: After maintenance label + weight bump p99 is back to ~700ms at 19:47. Streaming stalls largely resolved.
Dan O'Neill: Root cause: policy rollout lowered effective capacity for a critical hash range (policy changed consistent-hash weight map). The change passed automation but removed ~30% capacity from pool handling hot keys, creating a hot partition. Also our guardrail doesn't currently simulate steady-state key distribution so it missed the regression.
Mira Patel: Immediate action items: revert/roll back the routing-policy change to previous stable (0.9.1) and add a release-block that prevents >20% capacity reassign without manual review. I'll open the PR.
Alex Chen: Rollback in progress: ```
# deploy
kubectl rollout undo deployment/router-policy --to-revision=0.9.1
```
Alex Chen: Rollback complete at 19:52 UTC. Monitoring.
Ryan SRE: Post-rollback metrics look stable. p95 ~130ms, p99 ~650ms, errors back to baseline. We'll keep increased monitoring for the next 2 hours.
Liz Product: Drafting customer comms: short note explaining transient latency, impacted window 19:23-19:52 UTC, affected customers list, mitigation steps taken, and next steps. Will share copy here for review.
Mira Patel: Long-term: add unit tests for routing-policy changes that simulate hotkey distributions, add a preflight capacity check, and require manual approval for capacity shifts >20%. Also add runbook update for 'routing policy rollout' to include KV cache warming steps.
Dan O'Neill: I'll take follow-up to add a metric that breaks down routing weight changes per pool in the release pipeline.
Alex Chen: Closing incident as mitigated at 19:58 UTC. p99 under SLO, streaming stable. Assigning follow-ups: Mira -> preflight guardrails, Dan -> pipeline metric, Ryan -> post-incident monitoring alert thresholds, Liz -> customer note and RCA.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED by Alex Chen (duration ~35m). Postmortem ticket: https://tickets.redwood/internal/INC-2026
